analysis.title: Global Markets Outlook 2027: Growing Pains
key_insights: Goldman's 2027 baseline is friendly: stable global growth, declining inflation and peaking policy rates. Risks to markets are skewed to the downside because the market cycle is ageing, with higher real rates, wider credit spreads and rising volatility under the surface.

The AI investment impulse (additional AI investment as a share of GDP) is forecast to peak in early 2027. Goldman calls this manageable for the economy but a bigger test for markets, because AI contributed far more to earnings and market value growth than to GDP growth.
AI infrastructure beneficiaries have already de-rated since June. The open question is whether record S&P 500 earnings relative to GDP prove persistent as the investment cycle fades.
S&P 500 earnings growth is forecast to slow from 36% in 2026 to 11% in 2027. Goldman says this should limit the de-rating of AI-exposed areas but also means less relief in core rates pricing.

Equity leadership may pass from AI infrastructure to hyperscalers (if monetization becomes visible), AI productivity adopters and non-AI companies that benefit from less crowding out of capital. The risk is that the handoff is slow or that markets look ahead to the investment share peak in 2028, turning a rotation into an aggregate shock. Financial conditions are the most likely channel for AI worries to reach the economy.

Energy: the baseline is a gradual decline in oil prices even without full resolution of the Iran war, since supply is largely restored. An escalation-driven oil spike remains one of the biggest near-term risks, and Europe is exposed this winter through low gas storage.

Oil hedge value depends on the risk premium. When the premium is low, as it is after the November decline, hedging value is higher. When it was very high at the end of October, outright oil longs were riskier than options. Faster resolution in Iran or Ukraine is a clear upside risk for broader markets.

Bonds: central bank pricing in the US and UK is judged too hawkish relative to the baseline. Goldman sees UST 10y yields at 4.6% by end-2027 and argues for higher bond allocations on running yield, cheap valuations and underweight positioning. Equity-bond correlations have turned more negative as the shock shifted from energy to AI.

Dollar: a roughly 3% fall in the broad trade-weighted Dollar is forecast for 2027 as inflation, energy prices and hawkish Fed pricing fade. The Fed is expected to move from hikes to cuts in late 2027 and early 2028. If US tech erodes, Goldman expects Dollar underperformance rather than a safe-haven bid, with JPY the better haven and CNY continuing to appreciate.

Europe and UK: French fiscal concerns are unlikely to be addressed before the spring 2027 election, so EUR downside optionality stays attractive and EUR is a popular funder. UK Gilts have the highest beta to oil and may gain most from energy relief. GBP is the most overvalued G10 currency and Goldman's UK policy forecasts are the most dovish relative to market pricing.

Credit: record credit and equity issuance to fund AI is being absorbed with discounted pricing. Goldman expects modest further widening in index-level US spreads in 2027, with a higher chance of meaningful widening than tightening, bifurcation between AI issuers and other issuers, and modest US HY underperformance. Europe offers more risk premium, and mortgages and structured credit offer refuge from corporate supply.

EM: assets showed resilience again in 2026, but valuations and carry are less compelling. The case is exposure to high, diversified yields in hard and local currency bonds (South Africa, Hungary, Colombia, India cited) and a diversified earnings mix in equal-weighted EM equities. EM local assets offer upside convexity if core rates or the Dollar fall more than expected.

Hedging: Goldman favors diversification into bonds and commodities, positioning for lower US and Japan rates, USD/JPY downside, European gas hedges and equity protection. Index volatility is unlikely to fall much and could rise if macro stress broadens.

sector_views.rationale: Already de-rated since June. Earnings growth stays positive in 2027 but the investment impulse peaks, so the focus shifts to sustainability of record profits.
Described as resilient and defensive with less tech exposure than the US, though they carry significant energy exposure.
Under pressure from the energy terms-of-trade shock and sovereign stress, but a small tech share means a better relative showing if AI spending slows.
Case rests on a regionally and sectorally diversified earnings mix, especially in equal-weighted indices, rather than the AI earnings surge in the headline index.
Heavy AI-related issuance needs discounted pricing, and further spread widening is likely with modest HY underperformance.

earnings_insights: GS forecasts S&P 500 earnings growth slowing from 36% in 2026 to 11% in 2027 (forecast, not reported).
S&P 500 earnings are at a record share of GDP (Exhibit 2), and Goldman questions how much of the recent profit acceleration will persist as AI investment fades.
Free cash flow at the hyperscalers has deteriorated sharply per Goldman, while balance sheets of major borrowers remain strong.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Goldman calls current levels cheap valuation for duration and sees only shallow rate relief under the baseline, with larger moves if AI spending slows faster.
Softer Dollar as US inflation converges to target, energy prices decline and the Fed shifts from hikes to cuts.
Deceleration from 36% in 2026 but still robust, which should limit the de-rating of AI-exposed areas.
Policy rates expected to peak lower than in 2023-2024 and reverse earlier. Goldman sees central bank pricing as too hawkish.
Baseline leaves energy and core commodity returns muted. Risks around the oil forecast are skewed to the upside.
Risks are skewed toward wider rather than tighter spreads, with AI-related issuers weakest.
A second-derivative turning point that can end the run of positive surprises even while growth stays positive. The investment share itself peaks in 2028.

trade_ideas.description: Long duration and larger bond allocations, positioned for lower US and Japan rates
trade_ideas.rationale: Higher running yield, cheap valuations, underweight positioning and more paths to relief as supply shocks give way to demand stresses.
trade_ideas.risk: Energy shock extends further or inflation stays stickier with a resilient labour market.

trade_ideas.description: Short USD/JPY (long Yen) as a hedge for pro-cyclical portfolios
trade_ideas.rationale: Yen is undervalued and typically performs when rates and equities fall together, with authorities focused on limiting Yen weakness.

trade_ideas.description: Long CNY against the Dollar, gradual appreciation
trade_ideas.rationale: Deep undervaluation and a growing trade surplus, with forward markets underestimating how far appreciation can run.

trade_ideas.description: EUR downside optionality, with EUR as a funding currency
trade_ideas.rationale: French fiscal concerns persist until the spring 2027 election, the skew of risks favors downside and carry is low. EUR funding also hedges energy upside.
trade_ideas.risk: Energy relief or lower global yields would help Europe.

trade_ideas.description: European gas futures and TTF call spreads as asymmetric hedges against energy escalation
trade_ideas.rationale: Low gas storage leaves Europe vulnerable to supply and weather risk this winter.

trade_ideas.description: Equity protection via out-of-the-money puts or replacing equity holdings with longer-dated call options
trade_ideas.rationale: Index volatility has scope to rise and the market cycle is maturing.

trade_ideas.description: Long UK Gilts as the most oil-sensitive DM rates market
trade_ideas.rationale: Gilts have the highest beta to oil prices, so energy relief gives the most help to UK rates and fiscal picture.
trade_ideas.risk: Oil spike would hurt Gilts most.

trade_ideas.description: EM local and hard currency fixed income, and equal-weighted EM equities
trade_ideas.rationale: High, diversified and resilient yields with improving fiscal stories, plus upside convexity if core rates or the Dollar fall.
trade_ideas.risk: Tight spreads and middling carry and valuations limit upside.

risk_factors: Oil spike from renewed escalation in the Iran war, which would hurt equities, lift rates and support the Dollar against European currencies.
AI-related drawdowns tightening financial conditions, or the market looking forward to the 2028 peak in the investment share.
The equity handoff from AI infrastructure to other sectors failing to happen smoothly.
Sticky core inflation or a resilient labour market keeping central banks hawkish.
Episodic indigestion of jumbo AI debt financing and weakness among weaker borrowers.
European winter gas supply and weather risk given low storage.
French fiscal stress before the spring 2027 election.
Oil risk premium swings that change the value of energy hedges.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 compares AI's contribution to growth in US GDP, US capex, US earnings and US market value, and Goldman's text says the contribution is larger for earnings and market value than for GDP.
Exhibit 2 plots S&P 500 total earnings as a share of GDP on a 4-quarter moving average, labeled a record share.
Exhibit 6 plots a Brent risk premium estimate with annotations for the ceasefire announcement, MoU signing, Houthi blockade announcement and US midterms.
Exhibit 7 plots 1-week and 1-month S&P 500/10Y US Treasury correlations, titled as showing more negative equity-bond correlations as the shift from energy to AI pressure improved bond hedging value.
Exhibit 15 is titled as showing real yields are historically high, both in absolute and relative terms.
vol_and_positioning: Equity index volatility has risen a little but is unlikely to fall much from here and has scope to rise further if macro stresses broaden.
The sharpest volatility so far has been under the surface of the major equity indices.
Deeper equity protection, either out-of-the-money puts or replacing equity holdings with longer-dated call options, looks more valuable than usual as the cycle matures.
Bond positioning is described as underweight, supporting the duration case.
Using the Euro as a funder for other crosses is a popular position, and the skew of risks and low carry make downside EUR optionality attractive near term.
Oil options have been safer than outright longs when the oil risk premium is very high.
geopolitical: Ongoing war with Iran: oil supply largely restored but risks of escalation and new supply disruptions keep a fluctuating risk premium in oil.
Possible faster resolution of conflicts in Iran and Ukraine is flagged as a clear source of upside risk for broader markets.
French election in spring 2027 is when underlying French fiscal issues are expected to be addressed.
Japanese policy authorities are focused on limiting further Yen depreciation and encouraging inflows into Japanese assets.
China's growing trade surplus and deep undervaluation support further gradual Yuan appreciation.
Chart annotations on the Brent risk premium reference a ceasefire announcement, an MoU signing, a Houthi blockade announcement and the US midterms.

tension_points.bull_case: AI investment and earnings growth stay firmly positive in 2027 (S&P 500 earnings +11%), and leadership passes to hyperscalers, AI users and non-AI companies as crowding out of capital eases.
tension_points.bear_case: The rotation becomes a bigger aggregate shock if markets look ahead to the 2028 investment share peak, the handoff is slow, or financial and credit conditions feed back faster than baseline.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Markets pricing the 2028 investment share peak early, a stalled handoff to other sectors, or a tightening of financial and credit conditions faster than the baseline.

tension_points.bull_case: Supply is largely restored and the baseline is a gradual decline in energy prices, with faster resolution in Iran or Ukraine lowering prices more quickly and supporting bonds and equities.
tension_points.bear_case: Another escalation in the Iran war or new supply disruptions could spike oil, hurting equities and bonds together and pushing rates up.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A broadening of the conflict and new supply disruptions would invalidate the gradual-decline baseline.

tension_points.bull_case: Running yield, cheap valuations, underweight positioning and shallow rate relief make duration attractive, and bond hedging value is returning as the shock shifts from energy to AI.
tension_points.bear_case: The energy shock extends or inflation stays stickier with a resilient labour market, keeping rates higher.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An extended energy shock or stickier inflation with a resilient labour market.

tension_points.theme: US credit spreads and AI financing
tension_points.bull_case: Issuance has been digestible, balance sheets of major borrowers are strong and the base case is only modest widening.
tension_points.bear_case: Jumbo AI debt issuance could cause episodic indigestion, and weaker borrowers in the left tail could make financing conditions more turbulent.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Economic conditions deteriorating more than expected or investors becoming uncomfortable about the profitability of the AI investment boom.

theme_stances.key_argument: The AI investment impulse peaks in early 2027 and is a bigger test for markets than the economy.
theme_stances.evidence: Markets have already de-rated AI infrastructure beneficiaries.

theme_stances.key_argument: Higher running yield, cheap valuations and more paths to relief argue for higher bond allocations.
theme_stances.evidence: Bonds reclaim macro and hedging value

theme_stances.key_argument: Heavy AI-related issuance needs discounted pricing, so spreads are more likely to widen meaningfully than tighten.
theme_stances.evidence: A further widening in US spreads looks likely
